question: Which of the following Articles deals with the amendment of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 368**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 368 of the Indian Constitution deals with the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and its procedure.
 
• This article provides the procedure for the amendment of the Constitution, which can be initiated only by the introduction of a Bill for the purpose in either House of Parliament.
 
• The Bill must be passed in each House by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members of that House present and voting.
 
• Some amendments require the additional ratification by at least one-half of the State Legislatures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 360**

 
 
• Article 360 empowers the President of India to proclaim a Financial Emergency if he/she believes that the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.
 
• During Financial Emergency, the executive authority of the Union extends to the giving of directions to any State to observe such canons of financial propriety as may be specified in the directions, and such other measures as the President may deem necessary.
 
 
 
• **Article 352**
 
 
• Article 352 empowers the President to declare a National Emergency when the security of India or any part of it is threatened by war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• Such an emergency can alter the federal structure of the country to a unitary one.
 
 
 
• **Article 356**
 
 
• Article 356, often referred to as President's Rule, deals with the failure of the constitutional machinery in a State.
 
• It allows the President to assume the functions of the State Government and/or to dissolve the State legislative assembly if the State government is unable to function according to the provisions of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Article 368**
 
 
• Article 368 gives the Parliament the power to amend the Constitution and its procedure.
 
• This power is not absolute and is subject to the judicial review of the Supreme Court.
 
• Amendments can be classified into three categories: simple majority, special majority, and special majority with the ratification of states.
 
• Important amendments include the 42nd Amendment (which brought significant changes to the Constitution) and the 44th Amendment (which restored certain powers to the judiciary and reduced the power of the executive).
